clue.text: Joggers set swan off, keeping fit backfired

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
off means wrong or awry, so the letters of set swan are rearranged
backfired suggests going into reverse, so the synonym for fit is read backwards

parts.note: fit means apt, suitable

explanation.surface: Someone tried to get fit by setting a swan loose, and it went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters to SWEANTS; 'backfired' and 'keeping' do the rest. 'Joggers' looks like runners but is the trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Joggers are loose casual trousers for exercise, the same garment as tracksuit bottoms.

clue.text: Recognised spades as bladed items

parts.note: recognised in the sense of noticed or spotted, past tense of see
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Someone identifies spades as cutting tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Saws are cutting tools with toothed blades, so they are bladed items.

clue.text: Qualified journalist pens story with fellow that must be new

indicators.note: pens means encloses, as an animal is penned, so the journalist goes round the rest

parts.note: ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: the fellow must be replaced by new, so one letter in the story is swapped for another

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story
F is an abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A qualified reporter writes a story in which a male character must be a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that must be' swaps the fellow's letter for new; 'pens' wraps the journalist round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enabled means made able or empowered to do something, so it is a synonym of qualified.

clue.text: Start of row between loved ones in banker's office

indicators.note: between means placed among the letters of the loved ones, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: treasures are cherished people, as in calling someone a treasure

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the word row

parts.note: in means fashionable, the same as hip

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out between sweethearts at a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of' takes the first letter of row, and 'between' sets it among the loved ones; 'row' suggests a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of treasurer is the post of the person who manages funds, much like a banker's position.

clue.text: Vocal person likely to succeed, natural and upwardly mobile

indicators.note: vocal means spoken out, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: an heir is the person likely to succeed to a title or estate; natural means born, as in a born leader

explanation.surface: A talkative high achiever, natural and climbing socially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal' covers both pieces, HEIR and BORN together, which sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne is aloft in flight, literally moving upward, a cryptic sense of the social phrase.

clue.text: Lower head in ceremonial style

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering the head means moving the top letter further down the word

parts.note: a state occasion is a ceremonial one, so state is an adjective meaning ceremonial

explanation.surface: Bow your head in a dignified manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower head' moves the S of STATE two places down to give TASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste can mean refined aesthetic judgement or flair, close to having style.

clue.text: Exhibit open to view in auditorium

indicators.note: in an auditorium things are heard, so the word for open to view is replaced by one sounding alike

parts.note: bare means uncovered or exposed

explanation.surface: A museum piece is on display in a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a mark or sign is to show or display it, a synonym of exhibit as a verb.

clue.text: Slippery base on vessel with drip therein

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the base comes first

parts.note: E is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: therein means inside it, so the drip goes into the vessel

parts.note: a vase is a decorative vessel
IV is an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A slippery hospital scene: a vase with an intravenous drip inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'therein' makes VASIVE, and 'on' puts the base above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone evasive dodges questions and is hard to pin down, which is slippery.

clue.text: Naively optimistic, tried on tight restricting ensemble

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the rearranged letters go round the ensemble
tight means drunk, so the letters of tried on stagger into a new order

parts.note: a set is an ensemble, a group of things that go together

explanation.surface: A tight outfit has been tried on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' rearranges TRIED ON to ROINTED; 'restricting' wraps that round SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing through rose-tinted spectacles is the idiom for an overly hopeful view, unrealistically cheerful.

clue.text: Wide, blooming large creature

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide
blooming in health means hale, fit and well

explanation.surface: A broad, flourishing big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales are the largest animals on earth, so a large creature is a fair description.

clue.text: Note twin tucked into sibling's leftovers

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: tucked into means placed within, so the twin goes inside the sibling

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a sibling; the possessive is ignored
twin as an adjective means dual, paired

explanation.surface: A note about a twin eating their sister's leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: Residuals are what remains after the main part is gone, so remnants or leftovers.

clue.text: Broadcasting House people needing inspectors at the top

indicators.note: in a down entry at the top means placed first, before the other pieces

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, so DIS are inspectors
a semi is a semi-detached house, very common in Britain
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Broadcasting House, the BBC headquarters, needs inspectors in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcasting House is the BBC's London headquarters, so the first two words look like one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissemination is spreading information widely, the sense of broadcasting news.

clue.text: Blast shelter is soon to be cleaned out

indicators.note: a blast scatters things, so the letters of shelter is soon are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: The bomb shelter is about to be emptied and swept.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose all your money, being financially wiped out.

clue.text: Low fruit agricultural worker gathered in drum

indicators.note: what the eardrum gathers is heard, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds alike

parts.note: a melon is a fruit, such as a Galia or honeydew; a collie is a farm sheepdog, a working animal on the land

explanation.surface: A downbeat farmhand collects fruit into a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker is a sheepdog, not a person; 'drum' is the eardrum, which takes in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low means being sad and depressed, the same mood as gloom.

clue.text: Small space in stable …

parts.note: an en is a printer's small spacing unit, half an em
in meaning during, as in in the night

explanation.surface: A little room inside a horse's stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a building for horses but is the adjective meaning lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring lasts and stays firm, so it is stable and long-lived.

clue.text: … humble servant of God requiring space inside

indicators.note: inside means within the other piece, so the space is put into the clergyman

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric, a servant of God
an em is a printer's spacing unit

explanation.surface: Continuing the stable scene: a humble cleric needs room inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower or degrade them, which is to humble them as a verb.

clue.text: Engineer admits no exalted status

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the letters of admits no are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An engineer confesses to having no high standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintdom is the condition of being a saint, a revered and elevated rank.

clue.text: Say something worthy about king

indicators.note: about means around, so something worthy goes round the king

parts.note: an asset is something valuable or worthwhile
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone speaks well of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state firmly, so it is a synonym of say.

clue.text: Bizarre uniform on bishop in Cork

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the pieces go into the stopper

parts.note: a cork is a stopper, which seals a bottle

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so uniform comes before bishop

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: An odd outfit worn by a bishop in the Irish city of Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city but is a stopper, a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means dreamlike and strange, so bizarre is a close synonym.

clue.text: Unsteady on nets after losing heart

indicators.note: nets means catches or encloses, so the first piece captures the second

parts.note: on in the sense of feasible, as in the deal is on, means viable

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle of the word after is dropped, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: Someone shaky in the cricket nets after losing their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' keeps only the ends of 'after'; 'nets' means captures. 'on' is the hard step: an event that is on is viable.
explanation.definitionFit: Variable means changeable, not fixed, and so unsteady.

clue.text: Chemical element upset stomach in clergyman pre-op

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the stomach goes inside the shortened clergyman
pre-op means what comes before op, so the clergyman loses those final letters

parts.note: a bishop is a senior clergyman

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads upward

parts.note: tum is a colloquial word for stomach

explanation.surface: A chemical upsets a clergyman's stomach before his operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pre-op' leaves BISH, the part of the clergyman before OP; 'upset' turns the stomach upward, and 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bismuth is a heavy metallic element, number 83, a chemical element.

clue.text: Sibyl, popular one brought in to convey answer for ancients

indicators.note: brought in means introduced inside, so these pieces go into the others

parts.note: to cart is to carry or convey
a sibyl is a prophetess, here a hag or witch
in means popular, fashionable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prophetess, a celebrity, helps give the answer about the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in to' places the first three pieces between the two that follow; 'Sibyl' looks like a name but is the witch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carthaginians were the people of ancient Carthage, rivals of Rome, so a people of antiquity.

clue.text: Although odd, short plastic hat provides shade

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of although are scrambled
short of means lacking, so the letters of hat are subtracted
plastic means mouldable, so the letters of hat can be taken out in any order

explanation.surface: An unusual plastic hat gives shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H, A and T out of ALTHOUGH and rearrange the remaining LOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost or spirit of the dead, and a ghoul is a similar spectre.

clue.text: Anatomical part that would be rotating inside wing

parts.words: that would be rotating inside wing
parts.note: put inside the word wing, this body part makes a word meaning turning in circles

explanation.surface: A body part that would be spinning in a bird's wing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer goes between W and ING of wing, and the result means rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: The heel is the rounded back of the foot, a part of the body.

clue.text: Unwanted reminder about upper-class being too conceited

indicators.note: about means around, so the reminder goes round upper-class

parts.note: an overprod would be one nudge too many, a whimsical coinage for an unwanted reminder

explanation.surface: A nagging note about posh people being too vain.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERPROD is not a dictionary word: it is built like overdo, an excessive prod.
explanation.definitionFit: Overproud means excessively proud, which is the same as too conceited.

clue.text: Recalled stuffing in Manchester United's season

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
stuffing means what fills the inside, so the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A recalled football season at Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing' takes ERUNI from inside 'Manchester United's'; 'Recalled' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To season someone is to toughen them by experience, as seasoned troops are hardened, so it is a verb here.

clue.text: 19 blazes in East End roar

parts.note: 19 across is variable, and Y is a typical algebraic variable
blazes means hell, as in go to blazes, and a Cockney from London's East End drops the H

explanation.surface: Fires in the East End of London cause a roar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to shout loudly, a synonym of roar.

clue.text: Strange man, but he'll cook

indicators.note: strange means unusual or odd, so the letters of man but he'll are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd fellow, but a good cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Heston Blumenthal is a British TV chef known for eccentric, scientific cooking, which suits the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity chef famous for unusual experimental dishes fits a strange man who cooks.
